🤯 Tired of Typing LaTeX Equations? 🚀 Built a macOS App for Screenshot-to-LaTeX OCR While web converters exist, I found the workflow slow (screenshot, upload, and copy). To fix this, I built LaTeX OCR, a native macOS menu bar app designed for speed and seamless integration. Why Native is Easier & Faster: - Always Ready: It lives in your menu bar, instantly accessible. - Instant Capture: Use a global shortcut (or menu click) the moment you want to convert an image to LaTeX – no browser needed. - Streamlined Workflow: Captures, converts, and copies to your clipboard in one go. Much faster than web upload/convert cycles. How it Works: 1. Hit your shortcut & select a region on the screen. 2. The app sends it to the Google Gemini API for highly accurate LaTeX conversion (requires a free API key from Google). 3. The LaTeX code is instantly copied to your clipboard. 4. (It also handles standard text OCR using Apple Vision.) Other Features: - Customizable global keyboard shortcuts. - Recent capture history in the menu bar. - Formatting options for copied text. - Lightweight & Open Source (MIT License). If you want a significantly faster, highly accurate, and more integrated way to get equations into LaTeX compared to web tools, check out the Github: https://lnkd.in/gcdX_Nfy ...more

We've been meeting more and more young builders who want to dive into deep tech. But unlike B2B saas, there's a lot more that goes into building the next big company in robotics, energy infrastructure, material science, biotech, space tech and more. So at Comma Capital , we’ve launched our Deep Tech Fellowship to demystify what it takes to build a deep tech startup for students, new grads and young builders. This September, we’ll have weekly online sessions with top founders, investors and industry leaders that can speak to what it takes to build, fund and grow a deep tech company. Our sessions will cover: 📝 How to take an idea from a lab to your first client 📐 Building a high-quality supply chain from scratch 📲 Finding the right co-founders and advisors 🚀 How to design a deep tech project to be VC-backable If you’re curious about the mechanics of founding a company in deep tech and want to leave with a realistic, step-by-step roadmap to do so: we look forward to receiving your application. Comment ‘Deep Tech’ below and I’ll send the link to apply. Months of planning means smooth sailing on event day, right? As Co-Commissioner leading this year’s 𝗪𝗮𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗹𝗼𝗼 𝗘𝗻𝗴𝗶𝗻𝗲𝗲𝗿𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗖𝗼𝗺𝗽𝗲𝘁𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 (WEC), the answer was surprisingly… YES (mostly). This weekend, I hosted the WEC alongside my amazing co-commissioner Eileen Kuang , welcoming over 150 students across 6 different competition streams, with the winners advancing to the Ontario Engineering Competition (OEC)! With an event of this scale, little hiccups are always expected. From super gluing the kiddie pool to serving 200+ hungry engineers, I couldn't have asked for a better team to handle it. 𝗠𝘆 𝗯𝗶𝗴𝗴𝗲𝘀𝘁 𝘁𝗮𝗸𝗲𝗮𝘄𝗮𝘆 𝗳𝗿𝗼𝗺 𝗹𝗲𝗮𝗱𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗪𝗘𝗖? 𝗦𝘁𝗼𝗽 𝘀𝗽𝗿𝗶𝗻𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘂𝗽 𝟲 𝗳𝗹𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁𝘀 𝗼𝗳 𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗶𝗿𝘀. In the beginning, I was running from room to room, trying to check on the competitions, food and judges all at once. I quickly realized: 1. That isn't physically possible 2. I have an incredible team for a reason Once I stepped back and trusted our prep work, everything ran smoothly. The team completely owned their roles, solved problems instantly, and crushed it. I learned that being a good leader isn't about trying to manage every moving part. Instead, it's about building a system that works and trusting your team to execute. HUGE thank you to the awesome directors: Lennart , Jane, Kai , Steven , Awais , Angela Zhao , Jacob , Shagun , Doris , Angela Zhou , Elaine , Julie , Kian , Kennice , Mikayla , Amariah BIGGEST thank you to the VPXs Anupra and Lauren for the constant support and guidance! And thank you to all the judges for your dedication and expertise!
